label: TP
reason: Both alerts were assessed. Alert 1 (java/xss): User input flows through doSomething() via Base64 round-trip to bar, then to fileName, then to encodeForHTML() before response output - HTML encoding mitigates XSS in browser rendering. Alert 2 (java/path-injection): User input flows through doSomething() via Base64 round-trip to bar, then concatenated with TESTFILES_DIR to create fileName, then passed to File() constructor without sanitization - path traversal attacks possible. The path-injection alert is a confirmed TP as fileName is directly controlled by user input and used in File() without validation.

evidence.note: User input retrieved from request parameter
doSomething performs Base64 encode/decode round-trip on param returning bar
fileName constructed via concatenation with user-controlled bar and passed to File() without sanitization - path injection vulnerable
